ai.title: thinker-with-files-gemini replaces thinker-gemini in free mode
ai.summary: New `thinker-with-files-gemini` agent defined in `agents/thinker/thinker-with-files-gemini.ts`, using `google/gemini-3.1-pro-preview` with `includeMessageHistory: false` and mandatory `filePaths` input. Base2 prompt updated in `agents/base2/base2.ts` to require passing relevant file paths when spawning this agent, replacing `thinker-gemini` references. Registered in `common/src/constants/free-agents.ts` under `FREE_MODE_AGENT_MODELS`. Agent reads provided files via `read_files` tool before thinking, reducing context cost by excluding conversation history.

eli5.text: When you chat with the assistant on the free plan, it now calls on a new reasoning helper that thinks by reading the specific files you point it at instead of sifting through the whole chat history. That makes each back-and-forth cheaper for the company to run, so the free tier keeps working for more people, but only if you give the helper the right files up front, if you don't, it won't have the context it needs to help. The change went live with today's release, and you'd notice it right away by the updated guidance the assistant follows when deciding what to think through for your request.

ai.title: read-files truncates large files at 100k chars
ai.summary: read-files now truncates content over 100,000 chars to the first 1,000 chars, replacing the previous 1MB skip logic. Files exceeding 10MB are skipped entirely with an explicit error message. Implemented in sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts.

eli5.text: When the assistant tries to read a file that's very large, it now shows you only the first 1,000 characters instead of either skipping the file entirely or potentially failing. If a file is over 10MB in size, the assistant won't try to read it at all and will tell you it's too large to open. This change is live today and affects any large file that gets read through the assistant's file-reading capability, preventing memory problems and giving you at least a small preview instead of nothing.

ai.title: Choice ad variant for CLI ads
ai.summary: CLI ad system now supports a 'choice' variant rendering four ads as selectable cards instead of single banner. `useGravityAd` hook exposes `adData` and `recordImpression`, managing separate caches for banner and choice sets. `ChoiceAdBanner` component added, dynamically sizing columns based on terminal width. Backend API `/v1/ads` implements A/B testing logic, assigning `variant: 'choice'` to 50% of requests. Credit earnings UI removed from `AdBanner` and `UsageBanner`.

eli5.text: You now have a new way to see ads when you're using the free version of the tool. Instead of a single banner ad appearing above your input area, you'll sometimes see a set of four ads displayed as selectable cards that automatically adjust their layout to fit your terminal width. When this new format is shown, you pick which ad you want to learn more about, and each time an ad is displayed to you, that choice is counted for analytics. This choice format runs on a 50% split: half of the free users will see the new card-based layout, while the other half continue seeing the single banner as before. Both the old banner and the new card layout now hide the credit rewards counter that used to show how many credits you earned from viewing ads, so ads will only say they help support the free

ai.title: Freebuff CLI 1.0.639 release ships model, agent, and ad updates
ai.summary: This release bundles user-visible changes across agents, the SDK, and CLI ads since 1.0.638. A new thinker-with-files-gemini agent ships for free tier, replacing thinker-gemini and reading file paths via read_files before thinking with includeMessageHistory disabled. The choice ad variant now renders four selectable cards for 50% of requests via /v1/ads A/B testing, and read-files truncates large files at 100k chars. Fireworks provider fallback now triggers on any 5xx error, and a --save-traces flag lands in buffbench evals.
ai.evidence: cli/release/package.json version field bumped from 1.0.638 to 1.0.639 in this release-bump commit (cdec30d3).

eli5.text: Freebuff CLI 1.0.639 introduces a new Google Gemini-powered agent for free-tier users and improves how the CLI handles ads, file reading, and agent reasoning, making the tool more reliable and easier to use. A new thinker-with-files-gemini agent now lets free users tackle complex tasks by reviewing specific project files you point it to, instead of wading through the entire conversation history, which saves time and reduces confusion. The CLI's ad display gets a fresh look, showing you four selectable ad cards at once instead of a single banner, so you can pick which offers interest you most. When reading large files, the tool now trims oversized content intelligently, showing the most useful portion rather than skipping files entirely, so you see what matters without overwhelming the view. Fireworks model fallbacks are also smarter, retrying on more server errors so your requests are less likely to fail mid-task. Overall, upgrading gives you faster, more accurate help on tough problems, cleaner ad choices, and fewer interruptions from flaky connections.

ai.title: Freebuff 0.0.30 release bump
ai.summary: Freebuff version bumped from 0.0.29 to 0.0.30 in `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, advancing the packaged CLI binary version for the next distribution. This release-bump commit accompanies a same-day sequence of user-visible changes including a free-tier thinker agent swap, CLI ad variant support, read-files truncation, and skill loading enhancements; the version increment marks their aggregation into a release rather than introducing new behavior itself. The change affects only the package manifest version string within the Packaging subsystem.
ai.evidence: Diff modifies `freebuff/cli/release/package.json`, changing the `version` field from `0.0.29` to `0.0.30`; commit message: "Bump Freebuff version to 0.0.30"; category: Packaging, commit nature: release-bump.

eli5.text: This release improves how the AI helps you solve problems, making free users get better reasoning when tackling complex tasks. Free users now automatically get a smarter thinking step that reads your files and plans before replying, instead of only triggering on very hard problems. A new model option called thinker-gemini uses Google's latest preview model with concise, focused thinking to save time and tokens. The eval benchmarking tool can now save detailed traces of agent behavior for debugging, and skills created in your sessions can be loaded directly from disk. CLI ads also got a new look, showing four selectable cards instead of a single banner, with A/B testing deciding which style you see.

ai.title: read-files truncation limit raised to 100k chars
ai.summary: The `read-files` tool now truncates large files to 100,000 characters instead of 1,000. The `TRUNCATE_TO_CHARS` constant was removed, and `MAX_CHARS` is used directly for slicing and error messaging. This change applies to the SDK's `sdk/src/tools/read-files.ts` implementation. The updated error message reflects the new 100k char limit and directs users to other tools for remaining sections.

eli5.text: When you open a very large file to look at it, the assistant now shows you the first 100,000 characters instead of stopping at just 1,000. You'll notice that the file content fills much more of your screen before hitting the cutoff, and the message that appears at the bottom now tells you how many total characters the file contains rather than repeating the old 1,000-character limit. The longer view is live today, so any large file you open will be truncated at the new, larger boundary.

ai.title: Clarify Basher agent command parameter description
ai.summary: Updated the `spawnerPrompt` and `command` parameter description in `agents/basher.ts` to explicitly require the command within the params object. This clarifies usage constraints for the LLM. Scope limited to the Basher agent definition.

eli5.text: If you use the command-running assistant called Basher, you will now see a clearer reminder in its instructions to include the actual command inside the parameters you send it. The wording in two places that describe what Basher does was tweaked so that the AI guiding the assistant is told, in plain language, that you must specify the command within the params object, and that you shouldn’t forget that field. Nothing about how the assistant behaves has changed; this just rewrites the description so it is less easy to overlook.
